_doc: Content for the three concept-page rounds of the Sampler example: an invented site, 'Harbour Review'. Every key is explained in scripts/concepts/content.example.json. scripts/concepts/build-page.js validates this file; the templates read it from a JSON block and build all DOM with createElement/textContent, so nothing here is ever parsed as markup.

site.name: Harbour Review
site.lede: Photographs and notes from the quay: boats, weather, the café tables and the people who keep them, kept since 2019.

round.title: Two headline concepts for Harbour Review
intro: Georgia is the display face today. These are generated replacements, set by the same generator that will build the font, on the site's own colours, at the sizes the site uses, with real titles.
They are sketches, not fonts. Spacing, kerning and terminals are first-pass. Judge the voice, not the polish.

titles: A Field Guide to Wet Stone
audit_intro: The site was reviewed at 500, 1280 and 1600px before any letters were drawn. Each finding says what it changes for the font. The items marked first are the ones to fix before the face is chosen.

audit.finding: Small capital labels repeat the heading under them.
audit.fix: “Latest” sits over “What came in this week”; “Chapters” over “Four ways in”. Keep a label only where it adds a fact.
audit.font_effect: Large. With the labels gone, each heading stands alone, so the display face carries section identity by itself at 25 to 35px.

audit.finding: Boxed cards that lift on hover.
audit.fix: The four chapter cards rise with a shadow. Use photo, numeral, name and count, with no box.
audit.font_effect: The chapter names become the only structure, so the Bold at 18px matters.

audit.finding: Georgia cannot hold the 16.8px plate titles.
audit.fix: The plate titles look lighter than the body text beside them.
audit.font_effect: The hardest constraint: at 16.8px one screen pixel is 60 font units, so the Regular's thinnest stroke needs about 45 units.

audit.fix: The home page says “3 March 2026”; the grid says “2026-03-03”. Use one spelled-out date.
audit.font_effect: None, if dates move to the body face.

guidelines.lead: Differ from the body face in at least two ways
guidelines.text: out of contrast, stress angle, serif shape and width. Georgia is a sturdy text serif; a similar face looks like a mistake beside it.
15px chapter numerals, 16.8px titles in a grid, 25 to 35px section headings, 32 to 48px essay titles, an 80px title on cloth, and the wordmark in spaced capitals at 22 to 26px.
Regular and a clearly heavier Bold. The lowercase matters most: titles are Title Case, and only the wordmark is set in capitals.

guidelines.lead: Two character traps from the real titles:
guidelines.text: most titles hold a no-break space before the last word, and some type the apostrophe as a straight ' which must draw as a curly one.

text.desc: An upright, low-contrast bracketed serif with flared terminals: a text cut meant to hold the 16.8px plate titles with even colour.
text.risk: It is the closest to Georgia and is distinct from it by its flared ends and tighter fit. It is here as the control.

display.desc: The same drawing cut for large sizes: thinner hairlines, longer serifs and tighter spacing, so the 48 to 80px titles gain presence.
display.risk: Below 24px its hairlines fall under a pixel; it only works as the large half of a two-cut face.

recommendation.heading: Recommendation
paragraphs: Take both cuts to a second round as one face: the text cut for everything under 40px and the display cut above. Neither is a candidate on its own.
The lineup text box and the weight select above redraw every concept; the specimens below are fixed.

article.caption: An essay: plate 14, title, a section heading, and the Read next list
article.title: Bracket's Last Stand
paragraphs: The bracket in question held a shelf in the harbourmaster's office for sixty years, and the shelf held the tide tables. When it gave way on a Tuesday the tables went into the sink and the harbourmaster went to the café.
This is the story of the afternoon it took to find another, which is also the story of every shop on the front, in the order you would walk them.
article.heading: Three shops and a shed
article.paragraph_after: The chandlery had brackets but only in pairs; the hardware shop had one, bent; the shed at the end of the wall had six, in a biscuit tin, and would not sell them.

choosing.heading: Choosing
paragraphs: The tests for the choice: the face should differ from Georgia on at least two of contrast, stress, serif shape and width; it has to hold the 16.8px plate titles; and the Bold must be a clear step above the Regular at 18px.
Round 3 takes the finalists into the real font build, reviewed at each step.

faces.from: Text cut below 40px, display cut above

verdict.headline: What the reviewer says: build Sampler as two cuts
verdict.summary: The two-cut face is the only entry that holds the 16.8px plate titles and still has presence at 80px. On its own the text cut is plain above 48px, and on its own the display cut smudges below 24px.

items.text: Even colour at 16.8px, serifs intact at 48px, and the 80px wordmark gains the longer serifs. The switch at 40px is not visible on any page here.
Best at the 48px essay title and the 16.8px grid. Weakest at the 80px wordmark, the plainest of the three.
Best at 64 to 80px. At 16.8px its hairlines fall under a pixel and the serifs smudge.

verdict.next: Build the variable font with opsz 24 to 72 and the text cut as the default; measure where Chrome maps font-optical-sizing: auto with opsz.py before fixing the axis ends.
verdict.source: Review of 2026-11-15 from headless-Chrome screenshots of this page at 500, 1280 and 1600px. Unhinted rendering on one machine; Windows and phone rendering not checked.
